metadata.objective: Implement P2-06 source/ref resolution, schema-v1 SQLite evidence indexing, immutable bundle serialization and validation, runtime candidate activation and rollback, plus publication-last support without weakening the last-known-good or immutable-citation contracts.
metadata.dirty_state: non-Git shared workspace; pre-existing P2-00 through P2-05 work and user changes are preserved and cannot be attributed by Git

reasons: P2-06 joins durable SQLite/index data, archive security, activation lifecycle, concurrent handles, runtime state, and publication ordering at shared producer-consumer seams.
The host does not provide authoritative child-model identity or isolated worktrees, so a qualified worker package cannot own these critical contracts.

rejected_modes.reason: The candidate changes are all persistence, security, network, lifecycle, concurrency, or producer-consumer work owned by Main under the execution playbook.
No frozen, noncritical production leaf remains after Main retains the required P2-06 seams; read-only evaluation is sufficient additional review.

current_state_evidence.observation: Validated public configuration already supplies enabled repositories, ref, inclusion/exclusion policy, chunk limits, and the embedding identity consumed by the index builder.
Stable content-addressed E_ evidence IDs, normalized paths/content, evidence classes, and exact commit validation already exist; P2-06 must consume rather than redefine them.
The P2-01 pure classifier accepts bounded metadata and returns body-free inclusion decisions, but no production source-intake caller exists yet.
The P2-02 parser emits bounded deterministic candidates, but no evidence/database producer consumes them yet.
The P2-03 compiler creates only generated quoted FTS expressions or a short exact-value mode; the P2-06 reader must bind those values to both real FTS5 tables.
The P2-04 reader primitive validates frozen float32 unit vectors, dimensions, finite values, and stable ranking; the bundle reader must construct it only after manifest/database compatibility checks.
Mutable runtime.sqlite already contains the bundle_state logical table; no immutable index or active-bundle lifecycle owner is implemented.
The real FastAPI lifespan initializes runtime storage and exposes a SetupState supplier, but it starts no bundle poller or handle manager.

A public, licence-safe fixture configuration and repository corpus exist for real source-to-index and bundle producer-consumer gates; public fixtures intentionally contain no hidden evaluation oracle.

control_flow.failure_path: Safe build error with no stable-manifest mutation
Body-free skip record or failed candidate build; no bundle publication
Archive, checksum, schema, or smoke failure leaves release/stable manifest unchanged

control_flow.symbol: bundle_state -> staged verifier -> atomic active handle/pointer (new)
control_flow.failure_path: Candidate quarantine and safe runtime state update retain the active/previous known-good handles

control_flow.symbol: active read-only index -> bound FTS5 queries + ValidatedVectorMatrix + RRF
control_flow.failure_path: Readiness remains false or a safe unavailable state is returned; no partial activation

control_flow.symbol: immutable release asset upload/availability verification -> stable-manifest update last (new production workflow/client)
control_flow.failure_path: Any validation/upload/availability failure retains the prior stable manifest

invariants.statement: Only configured public GitHub repository/ref inputs on allowed hosts are resolved, and every indexed/config repository is recorded using one exact lowercase 40-character commit SHA.
invariants.enforcement_owner: Main-owned source resolver and index-builder validation boundary
invariants.prohibited_behavior: Using a mutable branch/tag/ref in database records or fetching a repository-content URL/redirect host outside the configured allowlist.
invariants.counterexample: A configured default branch resolves to a fake 39-character SHA or redirects to an unapproved host yet produces a source/index row.

invariants.statement: Eligible fixture source bytes pass P2-01/P2-02/P1 evidence validation into schema-v1 index.sqlite with dual FTS5 rows and finite normalized float32 blobs that the real reader can load and query read-only.
invariants.enforcement_owner: Main-owned index schema writer plus read-only bundle reader
invariants.prohibited_behavior: Persisting excluded/secret-like input, an unstable evidence ID, unvalidated embedding bytes, or writer-only output never parsed by the runtime reader.
invariants.counterexample: A P2-01 excluded .env fixture creates an evidence/embedding row, or a produced index cannot load through the real FTS/vector consumer.

invariants.statement: A bundle contains only the declared normalized regular files, canonical manifest and internal checksums; outer and internal checksum, duplicate, traversal, link/device, count, compressed/uncompressed-size, unknown/missing-file failures are rejected before extraction or activation.
invariants.enforcement_owner: Main-owned bundle serializer and safe staged archive verifier
invariants.prohibited_behavior: Extracting arbitrary archive members, following any link, trusting a manifest/checksum without bytes verification, or accepting an incomplete/unknown layout.
invariants.counterexample: A tar.zst with ../runtime.sqlite, a symlink, duplicate index.sqlite, a checksum mismatch, or an undeclared file becomes active.

invariants.statement: Only a bundle whose manifest schema, application range, index schema, declared embedding identity/dimension/prefix/normalization, required assets, SQLite quick_check, and real retrieval/card smoke check match the runtime becomes ready; its index opens read-only/query-only.
invariants.enforcement_owner: Main-owned candidate verifier and read-only bundle handle constructor
invariants.prohibited_behavior: Activating a schema/application/embedding mismatch, corrupt SQLite, failed smoke query, or writable index connection.
invariants.counterexample: A candidate with the fixture model but a one-off dimension/prefix mismatch returns a usable vector handle or readiness true.

invariants.statement: Download/staging/verification finish before one atomic active transition; invalid candidates and crashes before pointer swap retain the existing active bundle, in-flight handles stay usable, active and previous validated bundles are retained, and pin/unpin selects only retained compatible IDs.
invariants.enforcement_owner: Main-owned bundle manager, runtime bundle-state transaction, and handle reference counting
invariants.prohibited_behavior: Replacing/removing the active pointer before validation, interrupting an in-flight reader, activating an unknown/incompatible pin, or deleting the only known-good bundle on failure.
invariants.counterexample: An active A reader fails after B activation, a fault before the pointer swap leaves no A pointer, or a failed B changes active_bundle_id.

invariants.statement: Stable-manifest polling uses allowed-host URL/redirect validation, ETag conditional requests, byte/time bounds, and safe state diagnostics; 304 updates check time without downloading/activating and a failed check retains the prior active bundle.
invariants.enforcement_owner: Main-owned stable-manifest client and bundle updater
invariants.prohibited_behavior: Following an unapproved manifest/asset host, treating 304 as a new candidate, exposing private URLs/errors, or clearing valid state after poll failure.
invariants.counterexample: A redirect to an unconfigured host is followed or a 304 response downloads an asset/changes the active bundle.

invariants.statement: The index publication workflow validates/builds/tests, uploads one immutable tar.zst Release asset, verifies its availability/checksum, and updates stable-manifest.json only as the final mutation; every preceding failure preserves the prior stable manifest.
invariants.enforcement_owner: Main-owned publication workflow/client and mocked GitHub integration gate
invariants.prohibited_behavior: Updating the stable manifest before immutable asset availability or overwriting a Release asset in place after an earlier stage fails.
invariants.counterexample: A mocked upload failure increments the stable-manifest mutation counter or leaves a stable manifest referencing an unavailable asset.

invariants.statement: Identical normalized configuration, resolved commits, source contents, parser/chunker version, embedding identity, and assets yield stable evidence IDs, canonical manifest/checksum values, and declared-equivalent bundle contents; only documented build timestamp metadata may differ.
invariants.enforcement_owner: Main-owned deterministic index/bundle builder and P2-07 repeat-build evaluator
invariants.prohibited_behavior: Using unordered filesystem/database iteration, random IDs, local paths, or noncanonical JSON in identity/checksum inputs.
invariants.counterexample: Two builds from the same fixture inputs have different evidence IDs, hash suffix, SQLite logical records, or non-timestamp manifest fields.

invariants.statement: The committed Phase 2 fixture evaluation uses the real immutable builder, verifier, read-only hybrid consumer, and a separately stored expected-path oracle; it demonstrates Recall@8 at least 85%, paired zh-TW/en evidence parity at least 90%, and warm retrieval p95 at most 750 ms under recorded host conditions.
invariants.enforcement_owner: Main-owned Phase 2 fixture benchmark and reviewed controller oracle
invariants.prohibited_behavior: Scoring against expected evidence stored in the public fixture, bypassing the verified bundle reader, or presenting an unrecorded/local performance result as an acceptance metric.
invariants.counterexample: A public fixture contains expected evidence paths, a benchmark directly calls a retrieval primitive rather than a verified bundle, or one language in a pair retrieves no overlapping evidence despite a passing aggregate.

evaluations.phase_completion_claim: not made by the evaluator; Main determines closure from blocking gates and fresh evidence.

stop_conditions: Stop and ask the owner before changing a public API, environment variable, database/index schema contract, manifest/stable-manifest field, GitHub permission, provider fallback, asset layout, security posture, acceptance threshold, or v1 scope.
Fail closed and return to Main-only repair when a blocking producer-consumer, archive-security, compatibility, activation, or publication-last gate fails after one precise repair.
Do not call P2 complete until P2-07 independently proves repeatability, retrieval quality/parity/performance, and all required fresh falsification probes.

triggers: A dependency or lockfile change required for archive support
A package would require concurrent writes to a shared production seam
